Colour isn’t decoration. It’s direction. Especially in playground design. The right palette can turn a flat structure into an imaginative world. In India, where outdoor play areas compete with heat, noise, and concrete, colour isn’t a luxury,it’s a strategic tool.

Let’s explore how the visual design of play equipment can shape experiences, behaviours, and brand impressions.

Why Colour Matters in Indian Playgrounds

India’s sensory landscape is vibrant. Children grow up surrounded by bold festivals, busy markets, and colourful learning materials. So naturally, their play spaces should:

  • Stimulate curiosity
  • Encourage exploration
  • Reflect cultural vibrancy
  • Provide visual relief in urban spaces

The Psychology of Playground Colours

  • Red: Energy, excitement. Great for climbing or dynamic zones.
  • Blue: Calm and trust. Ideal near sand pits or sensory zones.
  • Green: Nature, safety. Widely used for toddler areas.
  • Yellow: Cheerful, helps with visibility and navigation.
  • Orange & Purple: Stimulate creativity and sociability.

Aesthetic Integration with Environment

Great playgrounds don’t shout. They harmonise.

  • Housing societies: Earthy or muted tones blend better with landscaped gardens.
  • Schools: High-contrast colours help younger children differentiate zones.
  • Malls or resorts: Branded palettes enhance visual storytelling and brand recall.

Example: A blue-and-white theme for a beachside resort or a jungle-green palette for a forest-themed school.

Material Finishes and Form Play

Aesthetics isn’t just about colour. It’s also about form and texture:

  • Rounded forms: Safer and friendlier-looking
  • Transparent panels: Add light and dimension
  • Texture-based play panels: Offer tactile engagement (e.g., sand ripple textures, stone finish plastic)

Use powder-coated metals, UV-treated plastics, and non-toxic paints for both beauty and durability in Indian weather.

Cultural Relevance in Playground Design

In India, themes like:

  • Animals (elephant, tiger, peacock)
  • Festivals (kites, rangoli, diyas)
  • Local architecture (temples, forts, rath)

...can be used subtly in form and colour to create familiar, rooted experiences for children.

FunPlay Equipment Designed with Visual Impact

  • Ulta Ghar: An upside-down house that sparks curiosity with bold geometry and colours.
  • Toucan: A tropical bird-themed structure using bright primary colours for engagement.

FAQs

Should play equipment use the same colour across all structures?

No. Using colour to differentiate sections by activity or age group improves navigation and safety.

Do certain colours fade faster under Indian sun?

Yes. Reds and yellows are more prone. That’s why we use UV-resistant pigments and coatings.

Can playground colour be customised to match school or brand identity?

Absolutely. Our modular equipment can be fully customised for your institution or project.

Are textured or form-based designs safe for toddlers?

Yes, provided they follow safety norms. We round off edges, use padded surfaces, and BIS-compliant materials.

Role of Government and NGOs in Reclaiming Play Spaces Across India

By FunPlay

In many parts of India, children have lost the freedom to play outside. Open lands are turning into buildings, parking lots, and garbage dumps. But play is very important for children’s health and happiness. Thankfully, the government and NGOs (non-governmental organizations) are starting to take action. Together, they can help bring back safe, clean, and fun spaces for children to play.

Why Play Spaces Are Disappearing

  • Cities are growing fast, and open spaces are being used for construction.
  • Many existing parks are poorly maintained or unsafe.
  • Villages lack proper play areas, especially in schools.
  • Children end up playing in dangerous or unhealthy places like streets or near garbage dumps.

This is a serious problem. Without safe places to play, children miss out on physical activity, creativity, and social skills.

How the Government Can Help

1. Protect Open Spaces
Governments should stop illegal land use and protect parks and public areas for children.

2. Build More Playgrounds
New town planning must include green play zones in every neighborhood: just like water, roads, and schools.

3. Maintain Existing Parks
Cleaning, fixing broken equipment, and adding lights or fences makes parks safer and more usable.

4. Create Inclusive Spaces
Playgrounds should be designed for all children, including those with disabilities.

5. Support Local Initiatives
Local government bodies (panchayats, municipal corporations) can support schools and communities that want to build their own play areas.

What NGOs Are Doing

Many NGOs in India are working hard to bring back play to children’s lives, especially in poor or rural areas.

Building Low-Cost Playgrounds
NGOs like Anthill Creations build fun, colorful playgrounds using recycled materials like tires, ropes, and wood.

Partnering with Schools
NGOs help schools design play-based learning areas so kids learn while they play.

Community Involvement
They involve local people in building and taking care of play spaces, so the whole community benefits.

Raising Awareness
NGOs also spread awareness about the importance of play in child development.

Working Together for Children

The government has the power and resources. NGOs have the passion and creative ideas. Together, they can:

  • Identify unused or abandoned land
  • Clean and prepare it safely
  • Design child-friendly play spaces
  • Educate families about the value of play
  • Most importantly, they can listen to children, and create spaces that truly meet their needs.

Let’s Make Play a Priority

Every child in India deserves a safe place to play. It’s not a luxury. It’s a basic need. With strong support from the government and NGOs, we can bring back joy, movement, and imagination to millions of children.

Let’s reclaim our spaces: for play, for health, and for the future.

School Playground Surface Materials: Which One Is Best?

By FunPlay

Introduction:
Choosing the right playground surface material is crucial for Indian schools. The best playground flooring ensures safety, durability, and cost-effectiveness, while supporting active play and easy maintenance. In this guide, FunPlay Systems compares top playground surfaces for Indian schools and shares expert tips for making the best choice.

When it comes to playgrounds, what’s underfoot is just as important as what’s overhead. In Indian schools, where safety, budget, and climate all matter, choosing the right playground surface material isn’t a cosmetic decision. It’s a structural one that directly impacts installation costs, safety compliance, and long-term maintenance.

Let’s break down the best options, their pros and cons, and which one fits your school’s needs. Looking to buy or upgrade your school playground? This guide will help you make an informed purchase decision.

Why Surface Choice Matters in Indian Schools

  • Safety: Prevents injuries from falls
  • Drainage: Helps avoid water logging during monsoons
  • Durability: Withstands daily wear from heavy usage
  • Heat Management: Avoids burns in hot weather
  • Compliance: Required for BIS and international safety standards

1. Rubber Tiles

Best for: Private schools, urban campuses, preschools looking to install premium safety flooring.

  • Pros:
    • Excellent fall protection
    • Available in bright, child-friendly colours
    • Easy to clean and maintain
    • Shock absorbent and weather resistant
  • Cons:
    • Higher upfront cost
    • Needs flat concrete base for installation

Interested in rubber tile installation? Request a free quote now.

2. Artificial Grass (Turf)

Best for: Premium schools, residential societies with shared playgrounds seeking lush, low-maintenance options.

  • Pros:
    • Looks lush year-round
    • Minimal dust or mud
    • Soft and safe for toddlers
    • UV stabilized: doesn’t fade easily
  • Cons:
    • Requires periodic brushing
    • Slight heat retention in summers

Need professional turf installation? Contact our experts today.

3. Sand

Best for: Budget-conscious schools, rural campuses exploring affordable surface materials.

  • Pros:
    • Inexpensive
    • Natural and soft
    • Great for free play and digging
  • Cons:
    • Can attract stray animals if not fenced
    • Needs frequent raking and cleaning
    • Poor drainage in heavy rains

Want to know how much sand setup costs? See our budget packages.

Tip: Use coarse river sand, not construction sand.

4. Mulch or Wood Chips

Best for: Nature-integrated schools, eco campuses looking for eco-friendly playground surfacing.

  • Pros:
    • Eco-friendly
    • Absorbs impact from falls
    • Aesthetically pleasing in natural settings
  • Cons:
    • Needs replenishing every 6–12 months
    • Attracts insects if not treated

Get a price estimate for wood chip surfacing. Talk to our sales team.

5. Interlocking EVA Foam Mats

Best for: Indoor play zones, kindergarten classrooms requiring safe indoor flooring.

  • Pros:
    • Easy to assemble and move
    • Great for floor games
    • Cushioned and soft
  • Cons:
    • Not suitable for outdoor installation
    • Can become slippery if wet

How to Choose the Right Surface

Factor Best Option
Budget Schools Sand or basic turf
Premium Schools Rubber tiles or artificial grass
Eco-conscious setups Mulch or natural earth
Indoor zones EVA foam mats
High rainfall areas Turf or rubber with drainage

Playground Surface + Equipment = Full Safety Setup

  • High slides or climbers → Rubber tile or mulch
  • Sandpits or swings → Sand or turf
  • Interactive play → Foam or rubber-based flooring

FunPlay Tip: Combine surfaces for a cost-effective hybrid layout.

FAQs

Is rubber flooring safe for Indian summers?

Yes. Our tiles are UV-resistant and tested for heat management. They do not crack or overheat.

Can I upgrade from sand to rubber tiles later?

Yes. Rubber tiles require a level base, so sand must be cleared and concrete poured first.

How often should school playground surfaces be inspected?

Ideally every 3–6 months. Loose tiles, water retention, or worn patches should be addressed immediately.

Do natural materials attract pests?

Not if they’re treated properly. We offer insect-resistant mulch and organic coatings.

Urbanization and the Impact on Children’s Play in India

By FunPlay

Cities in India are growing fast. More buildings, roads, and vehicles are coming up every day. While this growth brings jobs and homes, it also takes away something very important: open spaces for children to play.

Urbanization is changing how children live, learn, and grow. One big effect is that many kids in cities now don't have enough safe places to play. Let's look at how urbanization is affecting play and why it matters.

What Is Urbanization?

Urbanization means more people moving to cities and towns. This leads to:

  • More buildings and apartments
  • More traffic and pollution
  • Less land for parks, playgrounds, and gardens

In many Indian cities, parks are being replaced by malls, offices, or parking lots.

How This Affects Children

1. Lack of Safe Play Areas

Many children now live in small flats with no open space. Streets are crowded and full of vehicles, so it's dangerous to play outside.

2. More Screen Time, Less Physical Activity

Without open spaces, kids often stay indoors and spend more time on phones or TV. This can lead to health issues like obesity and weak eyesight.

3. Less Social Interaction

Playgrounds are where children meet, make friends, and learn to share. Without these places, they miss chances to build important social skills.

4. Mental Health Problems

Playing reduces stress and helps children stay happy. Without play, children may feel bored, lonely, or anxious.

Why This Is a Serious Problem

  • Children are growing up without a connection to nature.
  • They are less active and more likely to face health issues.
  • Emotional and social development is affected.
  • Poor and middle-class families suffer the most, as they can't afford private parks or clubs.

What Can Be Done?

Build More Public Playgrounds

City planners should include parks and green spaces in every new housing project.

Use Small Spaces Creatively

Even small corners or rooftops can be turned into fun play areas using recycled materials.

Schools Can Help

Schools should open their playgrounds after school hours for nearby children to use.

Involve Communities

People in neighborhoods can come together to clean, build, and maintain play areas for kids.

Promote Green Play

Encourage nature-based play using sand, mud, plants, and simple tools to make play more fun and eco-friendly.

Let's Make Room for Play Again

Urbanization is not a bad thing, but we must not forget our children in the process. They deserve safe, happy, and green spaces to play, learn, and grow.

Every child, in every city, has a right to play.

Let's build cities that care for their youngest citizens.

FAQs

How does urbanization affect children's play in Indian cities?
Urbanization reduces open spaces for children to play safely. As cities grow, parks and playgrounds are often replaced by buildings, malls, and parking lots. This forces children to stay indoors more, leading to increased screen time and reduced physical activity.
Why is outdoor play important for children's development?
Outdoor play is crucial for children's physical health, social skills development, and mental well-being. It helps reduce stress, promotes physical fitness, encourages creativity, and provides opportunities for children to make friends and learn important social skills like sharing and cooperation.
What can communities do to create more play spaces for children?
Communities can work together to convert small spaces into play areas, advocate for public playgrounds in new housing projects, encourage schools to open their playgrounds after hours, and create nature-based play spaces using eco-friendly materials. Local governments should also prioritize including green spaces in urban planning.

Using Natural Elements with Play Equipment for Immersive Spaces

By FunPlay

Using Natural Elements with Play Equipment for Immersive Spaces

What if the best play structure wasn’t man-made?
Imagine a playground where a boulder becomes a slide, a tree trunk is a balance beam, and a grassy slope becomes a rocket launchpad. Blending natural elements with playground equipment creates not only beautiful spaces, but deeply immersive ones.
Let’s explore how Indian schools, builders, and eco-resorts can use nature to level up play.

What Are Natural Elements in Playground Design?

Natural elements refer to anything organic, earthy, or unprocessed that becomes part of the play space. These include:

  • Rocks and boulders
  • Logs and tree stumps
  • Grass mounds and soil slopes
  • Bamboo, mud, sand, leaves
  • Water features and pebbled zones
  • Plants and shrubs

They can be used as stand-alone play tools, or combined with structured equipment.

Benefits of Integrating Nature with Play Structures

  1. Encourages Open-Ended Play
    Children invent their own rules with unstructured materials. A rock isn’t just a rock. It’s a throne, a step, or a fort.
  2. Builds Emotional & Sensory Intelligence
    Touching wood, walking on pebbles, or feeling grass helps children connect physically and emotionally with their environment.
  3. Reduces Screen Dependency
    When spaces feel alive, children are drawn outside without needing reminders.
  4. Blends with Indian Climate
    Natural materials are heat-resistant, water-absorbent, and often local, making them cost-effective and eco-friendly.

Design Ideas for Indian Schools & Public Spaces

  • Logs as Balance Beams
    Use polished logs (termite treated) laid horizontally or upright. Ideal for coordination and creativity.
  • Boulders as Climbers
    Place large smooth stones as climbing steps or seating. Double as gathering points.
  • Shrub Mazes
    Create exploratory paths with low hedges. Great for younger children.
  • Grass Slopes + Slide
    Instead of stairs, use earthen mounds with a slide on one side and log steps on the other.
  • Bamboo Fences and Forts
    Build simple nooks using tied bamboo poles and climbing rope.
  • Water Channels
    Incorporate water trickles or rain-fed rivulets with safety grading for monsoon play.

Pairing With Modern Equipment

Use natural zones between or around modular units:

  • Slide exits that land on grass
  • Crawl tunnels under trees
  • Sandpits beside climbing towers
  • Seating for teachers near green zones

FunPlay Integration Examples:
Paper Boat → Set in water-themed spaces with pebble borders
Toucan → Installed near flowering shrubs and bamboo fencing
Custom Log Paths → Designed around existing trees and landscape

Safety Guidelines for Natural Play Areas

  • Use treated, rounded wood to avoid splinters
  • Boulders must be stable and unsharpened
  • Avoid thorny plants or allergenic flora
  • Ensure soft landings with mulch, rubber base, or grass
  • Regularly inspect for termites, moss, or loose rocks

FAQs

Q1: Can natural elements work in urban schools with concrete campuses?

Yes. Use potted plants, raised earth beds, portable sandboxes, and bamboo dividers.

Q2: Are these elements more expensive than standard equipment?

Not necessarily. Local sourcing and minimal processing often make them more affordable.

Q3: Is this suitable for pre-primary kids?

Yes, with added safety measures. Use low-height, padded, or soft-edged versions.

Q4: Can FunPlay provide design help for nature-based playgrounds?

Absolutely. We offer hybrid planning that combines natural elements with BIS-compliant structures.

By FunPlay

Meta Description: Planning a school playground? Discover the essential features every school play area should include, from motor skill stations to inclusive zones and thematic learning units.

Playgrounds Are Classrooms Too

In schools, playgrounds aren’t just about recess. They're crucial developmental zones. Play areas promote motor skill growth, social-emotional learning, and even cognitive development. But for that to happen, the playground must be more than just a swing set and a slide.

Let’s explore the core components every school playground must include.

1. Multi-Skill Activity Zones

Every school playground should feature sections that encourage different physical abilities:

  • Climbing frames for coordination
  • Balance beams for proprioception
  • Slides for vestibular input
  • Swings for sensory regulation

Try: Bellatrix A compact yet modular play system that addresses various motor skills in a single footprint.

2. Inclusive Play Units

School playgrounds must cater to all children, including those with mobility, sensory, or neurodiverse needs:

  • Ramps instead of stairs
  • Tactile panels
  • Braille signage
  • Quiet zones for overstimulated children

Ask your manufacturer for inclusive modules built to BIS or EN1176 standards.

3. Thematic & Imaginative Play Areas

Encourage storytelling, role-play, and collaborative imagination with theme-based equipment:

  • Playhouses
  • Ships or castles
  • Mini marketplaces

Try: Ulta Ghar A quirky, upside-down playhouse that inspires curiosity and creative play.

4. Learning-Integrated Panels

Playgrounds can teach too! Integrate panels that reinforce classroom concepts:

  • Alphabet panels
  • Number games
  • Shapes and color matching
  • Memory and logic puzzles

Try: Phula Offers a multisensory experience ideal for primary school learners.

5. Age-Specific Zones

Segment the playground by age group:

  • Preschoolers: Soft, low-height sensory play
  • Primary: Climbing, cooperative games, logic puzzles
  • Middle schoolers: Physical challenge courses, team zones

Helps reduce crowding, accidents, and supports developmentally appropriate play.

6. Safe Surfacing & Materials

Must-have safety elements include:

  • Rubber tiles under swings and slides
  • Rounded edges and anti-tamper fixings
  • UV-stabilized plastics
  • BIS or international certification for materials

7. Weather Protection

In hot or rainy climates, consider:

  • Shade sails or pergolas
  • Drainage planning to avoid waterlogging
  • Anti-slip flooring for monsoon zones

8. Seating and Supervision Areas

Always include seating for teachers and caregivers:

  • Benches with clear views
  • Shaded zones
  • Paths with wheel access

Supervision areas reduce behavioral incidents and encourage safe play.

9. Green Play Integration

Link playgrounds to nature:

  • Garden patches
  • Butterfly zones
  • Tree log climbers

Use natural textures and themes like FunPlay’s Nature Sparsh series to balance concrete with calm.

10. Customization for School Identity

Add custom panels with:

  • School logo
  • Inspirational quotes
  • Color palette matching uniforms

This adds emotional ownership and branding to the space.

FAQs

Q1: What age groups should a school playground cater to?

Ideally, zones should be designed separately for preschool, primary, and middle school to ensure safe and appropriate play.

Q2: Can a school playground also be educational?

Yes. Panels with numbers, letters, and logic games help reinforce classroom learning in a hands-on environment.

Q3: How can schools include children with special needs in play?

By including ramps, tactile surfaces, quiet zones, and accessible equipment that follows inclusive design principles.

What Landscape Architects Look for in a Playground Equipment Manufacturer

By FunPlay

The Architect’s View of Playgrounds

Landscape architects aren’t buying just equipment. They’re crafting environments. For them, a playground is part of a larger spatial and emotional experience: woven into community parks, schoolyards, or urban landscapes.
So what does a playground equipment manufacturer need to bring to the table? A lot more than monkey bars and slides.

1. Site-Sensitive Design

Architects think in contours, drainage, sunlight, and flow. They need equipment that adapts to uneven terrains, maximizes shade, and blends with natural elements.
Standout: Toucan: A sculptural, organic play unit that sits beautifully in nature-integrated designs.

2. Customizability & Modularity

Standard catalog pieces? Meh. Architects want systems they can bend, tweak, expand, or shrink: based on the site’s dimensions and the user demographic.
Explore: Bellatrix: A modular marvel that fits snugly into urban parks, compact schoolyards, or sprawling gardens.

3. Aesthetic Compatibility

Visual coherence is key. Whether it’s a theme-based township or a minimalist city park, the equipment has to match the palette, textures, and vibe.
FunPlay’s Ulta Ghar is perfect for architects seeking playful structure with high visual recall.

4. Build Quality & Material Transparency

BIS certification is the start, not the end. Architects care about:

  • UV protection
  • Eco-friendliness
  • Powder-coated steel vs galvanized

Playgrounds are essential for healthy child development, yet many children in India lack access to safe, inclusive, and well-equipped play spaces. The Current Situation of Play Spaces in India

In cities and towns across India, open spaces are disappearing. New buildings, roads, and shopping malls are taking over the land. Playgrounds are either too small, too far, or not well-maintained. 11 October 2026 • Buying Guide

How to Choose a Playground Equipment Manufacturer in India

By FunPlay

Most playground tenders in India end up comparing three or four quotes that look alike on paper. Same photos of slides, same promise of "premium quality", prices that differ by 30 percent. The difference between them usually shows up two monsoons later, when one set still looks new and another has faded, cracked or rusted at the joints.

This guide is for the people who sign off on that purchase: school principals and trustees, builders and project managers, society committees, landscape architects and municipal engineers. It covers the questions worth asking any playground equipment manufacturer in India before you place an order, including us.

1. Find out whether they actually make the equipment

Plenty of suppliers trade imported or locally bought units under their own name. That is not wrong in itself, but it changes what you can expect. A company that runs its own design, moulding and fabrication can change a colour, adjust a platform height for a smaller site or supply a spare part five years later. A trader depends on someone else for all of that.

Ask where the factory is, what is made in-house and what is bought in. If you can, visit. A factory visit tells you more in an hour than any brochure. Our own plant is a 45,000 sq ft facility in Vasai, near Mumbai, where we do the design, roto-moulding and steel fabrication ourselves, and we are happy to show buyers around.

2. Check the materials, not just the photos

Indian conditions are hard on outdoor equipment. Strong sun, heavy rain, coastal salt air in cities like Mumbai and Chennai, and dust almost everywhere. Ask for specifics:

  • Plastic parts: Are slides and panels roto-moulded from UV-stabilised polyethylene? Thin or untreated plastic fades and turns brittle in a few summers.
  • Steel: Is the frame galvanised, powder coated, or both? What wall thickness are the posts? Coastal sites need better corrosion protection than inland ones.
  • Fasteners: Stainless steel or galvanised hardware lasts. Plain bolts rust and stain the paint around them.
  • Wood and rope: If the design uses timber or nets, ask how they are treated and how often they need checking.

A serious manufacturer will answer these questions in writing and put the details in the quote.

3. Ask how they handle safety

Safety is where cheap equipment costs the most. Ask which standards the designs follow. Many manufacturers work to the European standards EN 1176 (equipment) and EN 1177 (impact-absorbing surfacing), which are widely used as a reference in India. Then go further than the certificate:

  • Are there gaps where a child's head or finger could get trapped?
  • Are edges and bolt heads rounded or covered?
  • What fall height does each unit have, and what surface do they recommend under it?
  • Do they plan safe zones around swings and slide exits on your layout?

The surface matters as much as the equipment. Rubber tiles, EPDM wet-pour and artificial turf with a shock pad all behave differently. Our guide to playground surface materials for Indian schools compares the common options.

4. Match the equipment to the people who will use it

A preschool, a residential township and a public park need very different things. Ask the manufacturer which age group each unit is designed for, how many children it handles at once, and whether the range includes inclusive pieces that a child with limited mobility can use alongside friends.

Good suppliers will ask you questions back: the ages of the children, the size and shape of the site, how many families live in the society, whether the area is shaded. If a supplier sends a quote without asking anything, they are selling a catalogue, not designing a play space.

5. Look at the design and layout service

For schools and housing projects, the layout is often where value is won or lost. Ask whether the manufacturer will prepare a site plan or 3D layout, and whether they will work with your architect or landscape consultant. Builders should check whether the supplier can fit into the project schedule, because play areas are usually among the last items before handover.

Original design is also worth asking about. Many sets sold in India look identical because they come from the same few moulds. A manufacturer with its own design team can give a project a play area that looks like it belongs there. FunPlay's Originals range is designed in-house, and our team won a Red Dot Design Award in 2024.

6. Ask who installs it

Poor installation causes a large share of playground problems: loose footings, uneven platforms, wrong spacing between units. Ask whether the manufacturer's own team installs the equipment or whether it is subcontracted, how deep the foundations go, and who checks the finished site before children use it. For sites far from the factory, ask how they manage installation through local partners. We install across India with our own team or a trained local dealer.

7. Read the warranty and service terms closely

A warranty is only useful if you know what it covers. Ask for it in writing, part by part: frames, plastic components, moving parts like bearings and chains. Then ask about life after the warranty:

  • Can you buy spare parts, and how long will they be available?
  • Is there an after-sales contact, and how quickly do they respond?
  • Do they offer maintenance visits or a checklist for your own staff?

8. Check references you can verify

Ask for a list of recent projects similar to yours, ideally in your city or state, and call two or three of them. Ask how the equipment has held up and how the supplier responded when something needed fixing. Photos on a website prove that a project existed. A conversation with the facility manager tells you how it went. You can see some of our work on the projects page and the list of clients we have worked with.

9. Compare quotes on the same basis

Two quotes are only comparable when they cover the same scope. Before you compare prices, check that each one includes:

  • Exact models, dimensions and the number of users per unit
  • Material specifications (plastic, steel grade, coating, fasteners)
  • Safety surfacing, if needed, with thickness and area
  • Transport to site, installation and civil work such as footings
  • Taxes, warranty period and after-sales terms

A low quote often leaves out surfacing, installation or GST. Once everything is on the same sheet, the real price gap is usually smaller than it first looked.

A short checklist to take into your next meeting

  • Do you manufacture this equipment yourselves? Where?
  • What materials and coatings are used, part by part?
  • Which safety standards do the designs follow?
  • Which age group and how many users is each unit for?
  • Will you prepare a layout for our site?
  • Does your own team install it?
  • What does the warranty cover, in writing?
  • Can we speak to two clients with a similar project?

Talk to us

FunPlay Systems has designed and built playground equipment since 2002, for schools, housing societies, builders, resorts and public parks across India. If you are planning a play area, send us your site details and we will suggest a layout and a quote you can compare line by line. For more background, read our guides to playground equipment manufacturers in India and what landscape architects look for in a manufacturer, or browse the playground equipment FAQs.
